assertion: Assimilatory sulfate reduction pathways (I, III, and IV) are enriched in the duodenal microbiome of SIBO subjects (≥10³ CFU/mL on MAC) compared to non-SIBO subjects. Pathway enrichment FCs: 1.541 (P=8.25E-10), 1.6575 (P=2.87E-11), and 1.115 (P=.020825). Sulfate assimilation and cysteine biosynthesis superpathway also enriched (FC 1.14, P=1.00E-07). Assimilatory pathways I and III correlated with diarrhea severity (Spearman r=0.193, P=.031 and r=0.190, P=.033 respectively).

qualifiers.magnitude: Pathway I FC=1.541 (P=8.25E-10); III FC=1.6575 (P=2.87E-11); IV FC=1.115 (P=.020825); sulfate assimilation/cysteine biosynthesis FC=1.14 (P=1.00E-07); diarrhea correlation: pathway I r=0.193 P=.031, pathway III r=0.190 P=.033
qualifiers.conditions: duodenal aspirate; functional profiles from 16S data via MetaCyc Pathway Database; SIBO defined as ≥10³ CFU/mL on MAC
qualifiers.model: human prospective cross-sectional with predicted functional profiling

provenance.ref: Leite et al. Defining Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth by Culture and High Throughput Sequencing
provenance.location: Results — Gas Production Pathways section, p.266
provenance.original_text: Assimilatory sulfate reduction pathways (I, III, and IV) were enriched in subjects with ≥10³ CFU/mL on MAC vs those with <10³ CFU/mL (FC, 1.541; adjusted P = 8.25E-10; FC, 1.6575; adjusted P = 2.87E-11; and FC, 1.115; adjusted P = .020825, respectively), as was the sulfate assimilation and cysteine biosynthesis superpathway (FC, 1.14-fold; adjusted P = 1.00E-07). Furthermore, assimilatory pathways I and III correlated with diarrhea (Spearman r = 0.193; P = .031; Spearman r = 0.190; P = .033).

integrity.coi_detail: Pimentel lab (Cedars-Sinai MAST). Functional profiles are predicted from 16S (PICRUSt-style), not directly measured — inherent limitation.
integrity.methodology_note: Functional pathways predicted from 16S rRNA data, not directly measured via shotgun metagenomics for the full cohort. Shotgun data (n=38) confirmed enrichment of sugar degradation and pyruvate fermentation pathways.

chain_hints: KEY: These are ASSIMILATORY sulfate reduction pathways — distinct from DISSIMILATORY sulfate reduction (MECH-004/006/022)
Assimilatory pathways incorporate sulfate into amino acids (cysteine) rather than using sulfate as terminal electron acceptor
Both assimilatory and dissimilatory pathways can produce H2S, but by different mechanisms
Connects to MECH-004/006 (Desulfovibrio dissimilatory SRB pathway) — SIBO may involve different H2S production mechanism
Diarrhea correlation (r~0.19) is modest but significant — symptom link established
Supports breath H2S as a SIBO biomarker via mechanistic pathway enrichment
